evidence.field: 形義通解／甲骨、金文及簡帛字形；《說文》；金文用例
evidence.text: The database reports 備 forms in oracle bone, bronze, and manuscript scripts. It analyzes the early graph as 人 plus 𤰈, with 𤰈 serving as a sound element and depicting arrows in a container, identified with 箙, a quiver. The person facing away from the quiver is interpreted as carrying it, motivating preparation and readiness. It also reports bronze uses glossed as ‘equipped/complete’ and ‘for use’, plus loans for 佩 and 箙; Warring States manuscripts use the graph for words read as 服. These are source interpretations and reported readings, not independently verified readings of the image witnesses here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 備

evidence.text: The page quotes the Shuowen entry: 備, ‘慎也’ (‘be cautious’), 从人𤰈聲, and records 𠈍 as an ancient form of 備. It gives the Guangyun fanqie 平祕 and identifies the Middle Chinese initial as voiced bilabial with departing tone, third division, in the Zhi/Zhi rhyme categories. This is a transmitted lexicographic analysis; the page does not date the graph’s first appearance or establish that Shuowen’s gloss was its earliest spoken sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 備

evidence.text: The database cites a bronze-vessel inscription [冬戈]簋 with 備 used for 箙 in a list of weapons and equipment (‘戈、弓、備(箙)、矢’). This is a reported whole-graph loan for the quiver word; it does not establish that the depicted container’s own name or pronunciation is independently recoverable. The source does not give a date for this specific inscription in the opened entry.

evidence.text: For the component 𤰈, the database says the graph depicts arrows in a container, with the feathers exposed for access, and identifies the word in texts as 箙 (‘quiver’). search_audit.outcome: Opened CUHK 備 and component pages. The 備 entry reports examples for equipped/complete, for use, and whole-graph loans for 佩 and 箙. Its 𤰈 component page describes arrows in a container and notes 用 in some bronze forms, tentatively proposing it as a sound element.

search_audit.query: 备 简体字 1956 汉字简化方案 备 備 俻 草书来源
search_audit.outcome: Opened the reproduced 1956 scheme and verified its date, effective date and 备（備） listing. Search surfaced Wiktionary’s proposed 俻 derivation, but the scheme itself does not document that path. The government-hosted version was returned as a search result, not opened.

gaps: No original glyph image was visually inspected in this research pass. The CUHK page displays image links and form counts, while the Ministry page marks major palaeographic compilations as unavailable.

The CUHK textual view lists oracle, bronze, and manuscript forms but does not date the earliest attested graph or give the inscription dates for the specific examples cited. A secondary search result labels one oracle example 合565 商 and some bronzes by period, but that source page could not be opened; those dates are not relied upon here.

The earliest attested sense of 備 as a spoken lexeme is not established. Shuowen’s ‘慎’ is a later lexicographic gloss; it cannot be treated as the earliest meaning. The database reports earlier bronze uses for ‘prepared/complete’, but an inscription-level chronology and context review is still needed.

The semantic path from ‘person carrying a quiver’ to general preparedness and then completeness/all is a scholarly interpretation reported by CUHK; individual links are not all demonstrated by dated contexts in the inspected evidence.

A bronze graph 備 reportedly writes 箙 (‘quiver’) by whole-graph phonetic loan. Evidence does not independently recover the pronunciation of the depicted container’s own name; the sound match between 𤰈 and 箙 therefore remains unproven in this pass.

The component’s putative phonetic role in 備 is explicitly stated by Shuowen and CUHK, but comparative pronunciations for both 備 and 𤰈 in a single named reconstruction system were not retrieved. The supplied dossier gives Zhengzhang 備 *brɯɡs and 𤰈 *bɯɡ, but external verification here did not reach their primary character-specific source entries.

The dossier's Makemeahanzi account (夂 plus 田, farm/harvest) is unsupported by the opened historical references and appears to describe the modern simplified shape rather than the attested history of 備; it should not be used as formation evidence.

The claimed derivation 备 from 俻 by loss of 亻 is stated by Wiktionary, while the official 1956 scheme only equates 备 with 備. The specific variant-to-simplified derivational pathway was not independently established from a primary standardization source.
Opening the CText Shuowen page and Zdic graphic-history page failed with internal errors; no claims in this report depend solely on those pages.

The character’s earliest attested graph date is not established here. CUHK reports oracle, bronze, and manuscript categories; the Academia Sinica page identifies a Western Zhou bronze example, but no securely dated earliest oracle witness or first occurrence was verified.

The earliest spoken sense of 備 is not established. Shuowen’s ‘慎也’ is a received lexicographic gloss, not proof of the earliest meaning. Bronze examples reported by CUHK include ‘equipped/complete’ and ‘for use’, but full inscription chronology and contexts were not independently reviewed.

The semantic path from a person carrying an arrow container to preparedness, general defense, completeness, and ‘all’ is a source-proposed interpretation. The inspected evidence does not date every transition or establish the links as a chronological sequence.

For a proposed 𤰈 phonetic role, Shuowen and CUHK assert a sound role, and Baxter-Sagart independently lists 備 as *[b]rək-s. No independent character-specific historical pronunciation for 𤰈 was recovered. The source word for the depicted object is identified as 箙, but the object’s own original name/pronunciation cannot be reconstructed from the pronoun of 備; the sound match remains unverified.

CUHK reports 備 used as a whole-graph loan for 箙 in a bronze inscription. This loan does not show that the graph’s pictured object was originally pronounced like 備 or that the 𤰈 component itself had the same sound as 箙.

Some discussions may treat 𤰈 as an arrow container/pictorial source and others as a phonetic element in 備. The component’s semantic, pictorial and phonetic roles are not mutually exclusive, but the phonetic evidence is thin in the consulted pages.

The simplified graph’s official 1956 correspondence to 備 is verified. Wiktionary’s proposed path through 俻 has not been established as the historical derivation by the official scheme. 俻 is independently documented as a variant in the 1955 standardization list and by the Taiwan variant dictionary.
